newsitem.title: DUBAI: UK banks face retail challenge from supermarkets.
newsitem.headline: UK banks face retail challenge from supermarkets.

text.p: Commercial banks in Britain are facing increasing competition from supermarkets offering retail banking services, said John Langton, chief executive of the International Securities Market Association.

"Now in the United Kingdom...commercial banks are coming under increasing competitive threat from non-banks, while at the same time generating better profits than they have for decades," he told the annual Emirates International Forum in Dubai.

"I believe that this is the lull before the storm," he said, adding that profits of traditional banks in Britain and Europe were probably at their peak, and some supermarkets could in future turn in bigger profits from banking services than some banks.
"In the UK the Tesco supermarket chain now looks like it could well become the market leader in supermarket-based financial product sales," he said.
"I am in fact willing to place a bet that Tesco will, within five years, be making more profit out of retail banking than any of the traditional British high street banks.
"Financial services at the end of the day is a product line just like any other; one should endeavour to play down, rather than up, much of the mystique currently surrounding this area."
